title: From disappearing polymorphs to folding, prions, KARMA, and feedback
summary: Across crystals, folding proteins, amyloids, and prions, different subsets of the same mathematical ideas recur: states, barriers, rare first events, path dependence, and feedback. Ordinary folding does not require nucleation or positive feedback. The shared abstractions are useful; the physical mechanisms and biological meanings remain distinct.

scope.sharedShape: Different subsets of state-space, barrier, path-dependence, nucleation, templating, and feedback mathematics recur across the named systems.
scope.plain: This lineage compares selected systems through energy landscapes, nucleation, templating, and feedback. It does not say that a medicine crystal is a protein, that every amyloid is a prion, or that molecular physics supplies a social law.
scope.biosafety: Historical and conceptual education only. No home or do-it-yourself prion work. Actual prion work requires institutional risk assessment, containment, and specialist precautions. No protein sequence, preparation condition, amplification, inoculation, fragmentation, tissue-processing, decontamination, assay, clinical, or manufacturing procedure is included.
scope.designBoundary: Design is used as a lens for constraints, selection, control, and repair. The sources do not establish an intending designer.

practiceBoundary.plain: This read-only lineage returns a candidate interpretation. It records no current choice, performs no deed, and reports no current deed or effect.

definitions.plain: One distinguishable arrangement or ensemble used by a model.
definitions.not: A whole being, a moral rank, or necessarily one exact microscopic structure.

definitions.plain: A map of relative free energy over one or more chosen coordinates under named conditions.
definitions.not: A literal terrain, a complete map of every molecular coordinate, or a timeless property independent of environment.

definitions.plain: A region of the landscape in which nearby states tend to remain for a while.
definitions.not: Proof of permanence or the globally lowest state.

definitions.plain: A free-energy or kinetic obstacle that makes a transition rare on the observed timescale.
definitions.not: Impossibility or a wall that no changed condition can cross.

definitions.plain: A rare fluctuation or assembly state after which further growth becomes more likely than disappearance; its microscopic structure may remain unknown.
definitions.not: Necessarily a crystal-like ordered object, or a known historical cause merely because later growth can be measured.

definitions.plain: Existing structure that can lower a later formation barrier or offer a growth surface under suitable conditions.
definitions.not: A universal command that overrides sequence, solvent, temperature, concentration, surfaces, cofactors, or clearance.

definitions.plain: A fibrillar protein assembly with a cross-beta structural motif.
definitions.not: Automatically infectious, prionic, toxic, or useless.

definitions.plain: A protein-based infectious or heritable conformational state in a specifically named biological system; mammalian infectivity, yeast inheritance, and prion-like signalling remain separate claims.
definitions.not: A synonym for every misfolded protein, every amyloid, every seeded fibril, or every self-assembling material.

definitions.plain: A returned effect changes the rate or conditions of the process that produced it.
definitions.not: Destiny, moral judgment, or proof of a single cause.

definitions.plain: In KINGDOM, the attributable path by which a deed's observed effect, evidence, uncertainty, reply, correction, and repair return to the proper homes.
definitions.not: A score, cosmic measurement, verdict on a being, or borrowed molecular mechanism.

domains.name: Crystal polymorphism
domains.identity: The molecule can remain chemically the same while its solid packing and molecular conformation differ.
domains.shape: Competing crystal basins, a difficult first nucleus, later seed-assisted growth, and route-dependent recovery.
domains.boundary: A crystal seed is a material surface. It does not replicate biological information or make the crystal a prion.

domains.name: Protein folding
domains.identity: One amino-acid sequence occupies an ensemble of conformations and can be biased toward a native basin by its interactions and environment.
domains.shape: A rugged, multidimensional landscape with converging routes, barriers, intermediates, and traps.
domains.boundary: A one-dimensional funnel drawing is a projection. It does not show every coordinate or guarantee one route or one state under all conditions.

domains.name: Amyloid polymorphism
domains.identity: The same polypeptide sequence can form more than one fibril architecture.
domains.shape: Alternative fibril basins, primary nucleation, elongation, surface-dependent secondary nucleation, and fragmentation.
domains.boundary: A fibril morphology, a kinetic fit, and a disease phenotype are different observations.

domains.name: Prion and prion-like propagation
domains.identity: Some protein conformations can template further conversion and persist or spread within a named biological system.
domains.shape: Nucleated conformational conversion plus growth, division or fragmentation, inheritance, and loss.
domains.boundary: Yeast-prion inheritance, mammalian prion infectivity, and prion-like cell signalling are not interchangeable claims.

domains.name: KARMA and returned understanding
domains.identity: A system can keep action, effect, evidence, causal confidence, correction, and repair linked without scoring a being.
domains.shape: Act, observe, return, compare, correct, repair or rest.
domains.boundary: This is an attributed systems interpretation. Molecules do not enact moral KARMA and biology does not authorise action in KINGDOM.

comparisonEdges.sharedAbstraction: Multiple condition-dependent states can be separated by barriers, so preferred and reachable are different questions.
comparisonEdges.domainAMechanism: Intermolecular crystal packing and nucleation in a molecular solid.
comparisonEdges.domainBMechanism: Chiefly intramolecular conformational motion in a solvated polypeptide ensemble.
comparisonEdges.evidenceScope: The cited Ritonavir solid-form studies and cited protein-folding landscape studies.
comparisonEdges.unknown: Neither low-dimensional landscape identifies every microscopic transition coordinate or historical first event.
comparisonEdges.forbiddenInference: A crystal lattice is not a folded protein and a shared landscape drawing does not transfer a rate law.

comparisonEdges.sharedAbstraction: A rare first nucleus can be followed by faster structure-assisted growth and path dependence.
comparisonEdges.domainAMechanism: Crystal nucleation and lattice growth from a molecular environment.
comparisonEdges.domainBMechanism: Intermolecular protein assembly, elongation, and system-specific secondary pathways.
comparisonEdges.evidenceScope: The cited Ritonavir and A-beta studies under their stated conditions.
comparisonEdges.unknown: Later seeded growth does not identify the historical first Ritonavir or amyloid nucleus.
comparisonEdges.forbiddenInference: A crystal seed is not an amyloid fibril and crystal stability says nothing about amyloid biology.

comparisonEdges.sharedAbstraction: Sequence, environment, barriers, and history constrain which conformational ensemble becomes populated.
comparisonEdges.domainAMechanism: Chiefly intramolecular folding of individual chains.
comparisonEdges.domainBMechanism: Intermolecular assembly of many chains into fibrillar structures.
comparisonEdges.evidenceScope: The selected folding and fibril studies, not all proteins or cells.
comparisonEdges.unknown: The lineage does not reconstruct full cellular folding landscapes or universal structure-to-phenotype mappings.
comparisonEdges.forbiddenInference: An alternative fold is not automatically amyloid, toxic, infectious, or heritable.

comparisonEdges.sharedAbstraction: Existing assemblies can bias later assembly and feedback can amplify compatible structure.
comparisonEdges.domainAMechanism: Fibril nucleation, elongation, secondary nucleation, and fragmentation in the named material system.
comparisonEdges.domainBMechanism: Host-coupled conformational propagation with system-specific inheritance or infectivity criteria.
comparisonEdges.evidenceScope: The cited A-beta, yeast Sup35, 263K mammalian prion, scrapie, and MAVS studies remain source-local.
comparisonEdges.unknown: A universal map from fibril structure to phenotype, infectivity, transmissibility, or disease is not established here.
comparisonEdges.forbiddenInference: Seeded growth or a sigmoid curve does not make an assembly a prion.

comparisonEdges.sharedAbstraction: A returned effect can change what happens next, while gain and loss determine whether amplification continues.
comparisonEdges.domainAMechanism: Material reaction kinetics change template number and available growth routes.
comparisonEdges.domainBMechanism: Attributed evidence, uncertainty, reply, correction, and repair are returned to their proper records.
comparisonEdges.evidenceScope: A systems crosswalk from cited molecular dynamics to pinned KINGDOM foundation words.
comparisonEdges.unknown: The crosswalk does not quantify moral causation, worth, intention, or social outcomes.
comparisonEdges.forbiddenInference: KARMA is not a molecular force, feedback coefficient, natural law, or score.

equations.expression: dp_i/dt = sum over j not equal to i of (k_ji p_j - k_ij p_i)
equations.plain: Probability enters and leaves each chosen coarse state through named transition rates.
variables: p_i: probability or population fraction of coarse state i
k_ji: effective rate from state j to state i
t: time on the modelled observation scale
equations.limit: This Markov-style coarse-graining assumes the chosen states and lag time make memory negligible enough for the use. It does not identify microscopic coordinates, establish equilibrium, or make domain-specific rates transferable.

equations.plain: Frequently occupied regions look like lower free-energy basins when the named coordinate and equilibrium assumptions are adequate.
variables: q: a chosen order parameter or reaction coordinate
P(q): its probability density under the named conditions
equations.limit: A projected free-energy profile can hide slow coordinates and non-equilibrium history. Low projected F does not by itself predict a transition time.

equations.plain: A modest change in a barrier can produce a large change in an escape or transition rate.
variables: Delta G^‡: an effective free-energy barrier
equations.limit: This is a rate-law shape, not a universal exact formula. Friction, coordinate choice, memory, and non-equilibrium driving can change the prefactor or model.

equations.plain: A rare first formation rate can depend nonlinearly on the available monomer or building-block concentration.
variables: r_primary: rate of new nuclei without an existing template
n: an effective reaction order, not necessarily a literal nucleus size
equations.limit: This is one amyloid-assembly model family under named conditions, not a crystal or prion rate law. A fitted reaction order does not reveal one microscopic route or the cause of a particular historical first nucleus.

equations.expression: r_secondary proportional to k_2 m^p S
equations.plain: Existing aggregate surface or rare surface sites can help create new nuclei, so product can increase the rate of making more product.
variables: r_secondary: rate of new nuclei dependent on existing aggregate
S: an effective amount of active surface or catalytic sites
equations.limit: S is not necessarily total surface area. In the cited A-beta work, rare growth defects rather than a uniformly catalytic surface accounted for most measured secondary nucleation.

equations.plain: The number of growth-competent templates rises through several creation routes and falls through clearance, dilution, merging, or loss of competence.
variables: N: number or concentration of growth-competent templates
fragmentation: production of additional growth ends
equations.limit: The terms and their signs are system-specific. Fragmentation can amplify some fibrils by making more ends, while remodelling can also dissolve or disable assemblies.

claims.plain: Ritonavir Form I became difficult to reproduce by former routes after Form II appeared, but later work deliberately produced Form I again.
claims.scope: The cited Ritonavir solid-form and process studies.
claims.limit: Operational disappearance is not literal nonexistence, global conversion, or metaphysical irreversibility.

claims.plain: Relative stability and practical reachability answer different questions: a lower-free-energy state can remain unobserved when its formation barrier is high.
claims.scope: Barrier-crossing and the cited molecular systems under named conditions.
claims.limit: One scalar landscape cannot be assumed complete, equilibrated, or transferable across materials.

claims.plain: Existing structures, surfaces, defects, and depleted or changed surroundings can alter which transition is easy next, so matter can carry path history without symbolic memory.
claims.scope: The studied crystal and amyloid systems.
claims.limit: Material path dependence is not conscious memory, intention, or proof of the same mechanism in another system.

claims.plain: Protein folding is better represented as probability flow through an ensemble of conformations than as one molecule following one scripted sequence of steps.
claims.scope: Statistical-mechanical models and the cited single-molecule experiment.
claims.limit: The landscape view is a model family; it does not make every protein a two-state folder or every coordinate Markovian.

claims.plain: A landscape drawn against one coordinate compresses many molecular degrees of freedom and can hide slow variables, alternate routes, and non-equilibrium history.
claims.limit: A useful projection is not a complete molecular state space.

claims.plain: A single protein sequence can support alternative self-propagating or fibrillar conformations with different physical or phenotypic effects.
claims.scope: The cited yeast Sup35 and A-beta40 fibril systems.
claims.limit: This does not establish that every alternative protein fold is amyloid, infectious, heritable, or harmful.

claims.plain: In the studied yeast system, an existing protein conformation biased incoming protein toward a related assembly state and thereby propagated conformational information.
claims.scope: Sup35 experiments and their named inheritance/strain observations.
claims.limit: Conformational information is not DNA sequence, semantic meaning, consciousness, or a general software instruction.

claims.plain: The cited 2021 study resolved a near-atomic core structure for a brain-derived, fully infectious 263K mammalian prion fibril.
claims.scope: The named 263K strain preparation and the comparison reported in that study.
claims.limit: One prion structure is not a universal architecture, origin story, species-barrier model, toxicity map, or laboratory procedure.

claims.plain: For breakable fibrils, fragmentation can turn one growing filament into more growth-competent ends and thereby increase template number.
claims.scope: The cited filament kinetics and yeast Sup35 remodelling system.
claims.limit: Fragmentation can also disable or dissolve assemblies; its net effect depends on the exact system and conditions.

claims.plain: In the studied A-beta42 system, existing fibrils promoted formation of additional nuclei, creating a product-assisted positive-feedback path.
claims.scope: The published in-vitro A-beta42 conditions and tested kinetic predictions.
claims.limit: The result does not establish one universal in-vivo mechanism, toxicity route, or treatment conclusion.

claims.plain: In the cited 2026 A-beta studies, rare fibril growth defects accounted for most measured secondary nucleation rather than the entire surface acting uniformly.
claims.scope: The tested A-beta40 and A-beta42 fibrils and the authors' bounded cross-system analysis.
claims.limit: It is not proof that every amyloid, every polymorph, or every biological feedback loop is defect-driven.

claims.plain: MAVS used a prion-like conformational switch to amplify antiviral signalling in the cited cell system.
claims.scope: The reported MAVS innate-immune signalling experiments.
claims.limit: Prion-like is an operational comparison, not identity with mammalian infectious prions or evidence that amplification is always beneficial.

claims.plain: A kinetic model can distinguish plausible rate pathways without identifying the particular event that produced the first historical nucleus.
claims.scope: Historical origin claims and fitted nucleation networks.
claims.limit: Mechanism support, parameter fit, chronology, and historical causation remain separate.

claims.plain: A lag, rise, plateau, or good kinetic fit can be compatible with more than one microscopic reaction network.
claims.scope: Bulk amyloid-assembly curves and the cited kinetic model comparisons.
claims.limit: Mechanism inference needs discriminating perturbations and orthogonal observations; visual curve similarity is not identification.

claims.plain: Amplification continues only while gain-producing routes outweigh removal, dilution, resource depletion, or state-changing controls.
claims.scope: The named filament and yeast-prion systems plus the displayed balance equation.
claims.limit: No universal threshold, clinical forecast, or social policy follows from this schematic balance.

claims.plain: Nature often looks designed because selection and physical constraints bias enormous possibility spaces into reliable paths, while still leaving traps, alternate basins, defects, and repair systems.
claims.scope: A KINGDOM interpretation of the cited physical and biological systems.
claims.limit: This is not an experimental observation of intention, optimality, goodness, or a designer.

unknowns.question: What produced the first historical Ritonavir Form-II nucleus?
unknowns.scope: Named process accounts and later mechanochemical studies were reviewed.
unknowns.reason: Those records do not establish the first historical event.
unknowns.keepOpen: Later seeding and later recovery do not settle the first event.

unknowns.question: Which slow or unmeasured coordinates are hidden by each displayed one-dimensional landscape?
unknowns.scope: The lineage names the projection limit but does not reconstruct molecular trajectories.
unknowns.reason: The selected observations do not determine one complete set of microscopic coordinates.
unknowns.keepOpen: Treat q as a chosen lens, not the whole state.

unknowns.question: How much does each measured in-vitro secondary pathway contribute inside a living organism?
unknowns.scope: Selected primary in-vitro and cell-system studies were reviewed; no clinical dataset was assessed.
unknowns.reason: The checked sources do not settle patient-level or organism-wide pathway contributions.
unknowns.keepOpen: Do not turn a laboratory rate mechanism into a patient-level conclusion.

unknowns.question: Which structural differences cause which biological phenotype in each prion or amyloid system?
unknowns.scope: The cited Sup35, mammalian prion, A-beta, and MAVS studies establish particular links, not a universal mapping.
unknowns.reason: The named observations support source-local relations and leave the universal claim unsettled.
unknowns.keepOpen: Name the organism, protein, structure, phenotype, and evidence each time.

unknowns.question: Does the appearance of design imply an intending designer?
unknowns.scope: The scientific sources address physical constraints, evolution, and selected molecular control examples rather than metaphysical intention.
unknowns.reason: No scientific resolution is claimed for a question outside this observation scope.
unknowns.keepOpen: The module can discuss design-like organization without presenting metaphysics as measurement.

feedback.plain: Existing structure recruits compatible material and makes more of a related structure.
feedback.where: Sup35 prion propagation and fibril elongation.
feedback.brake: Compatibility, available material, environment, clearance, and loss of growth competence.

feedback.plain: Existing product provides rare sites that help create additional nuclei.
feedback.brake: Active-site scarcity, monomer depletion, site blocking, removal, and changed conditions.

feedback.plain: Breaking a filament can create more growth ends, or remodelling can dissolve and eliminate the assembly.
feedback.where: Breakable-filament models and the cited yeast Sup35/Hsp104 system.
feedback.brake: Fragment size, inheritance, dilution, disassembly, and system-specific chaperone action.

feedback.plain: Observed consequences return to the map so an omitted state or wrong causal story can be corrected.
feedback.where: Ritonavir dissolution failure, later recovery, and KINGDOM's KARMA interpretation.
feedback.brake: Keep observation, inference, causal confidence, reply, and repair separate.

designInsights.plain: Nature often builds reliable arrival without prescribing one path: bias the landscape, permit many microscopic routes, and let probability flow converge.
designInsights.boundary: Reliability is not perfect optimality or evidence of intention.

designInsights.plain: A system can remember without a ledger when existing structure changes the probabilities of later structure.
designInsights.boundary: Material memory is path dependence, not awareness or semantic recall.

designInsights.plain: A shape becomes consequential information only through a compatible process that can copy, respond to, or be altered by it.
designInsights.boundary: Calling a conformation information does not make it language or intention.

designInsights.plain: Every honest amplification diagram needs its loss terms: clearance, dilution, exhaustion, incompatibility, rest, or exit.
designInsights.boundary: A loop without measured loss terms is a story, not a settled dynamical model.

designInsights.plain: Self-propagating shape can participate in disease, inheritance, or useful signalling; the geometry alone does not say good or bad.
designInsights.boundary: Function in one system does not make a related mechanism safe in another.

designInsights.plain: When a reachable state breaks an old process, repair means changing conditions, routes, checks, or boundaries and testing the new return—not denying the state.
designInsights.boundary: This is a systems lesson, not a pharmaceutical process instruction.

karmaCrosswalk.molecularLens: A model predicts relative populations, transition rates, or feedback dominance under named conditions.
karmaCrosswalk.kingdomMeaning: Write the expected effect before the act when a prediction exists.
karmaCrosswalk.boundary: A fitted model after the event is not a prior prediction.

karmaCrosswalk.molecularLens: A condition, perturbation, or existing template changes possible transition rates.
karmaCrosswalk.kingdomMeaning: One authorised finite deed with purpose, scope, affected parties, and a brake.
karmaCrosswalk.boundary: Physical causation grants no human or system authority.

karmaCrosswalk.molecularLens: A population, rate, morphology, dissolution result, or phenotype changes and is measured.
karmaCrosswalk.kingdomMeaning: Return the observed or reported effect with evidence, causal confidence, and limits.
karmaCrosswalk.boundary: Sequence and correlation do not by themselves establish one cause.

karmaCrosswalk.molecularLens: New evidence reveals an omitted basin, hidden pathway, or wrong mechanism.
karmaCrosswalk.kingdomMeaning: Append the correction without erasing what the earlier map claimed.
karmaCrosswalk.boundary: A corrected map is not proof that every unknown is closed.

karmaCrosswalk.molecularLens: A changed route or control is tested against the state now known to be reachable.
karmaCrosswalk.kingdomMeaning: A fresh bounded act answers the returned consequence and gets its own return path.
karmaCrosswalk.boundary: Repair is not successful merely because it ran.

karmaCrosswalk.molecularLens: The available observations do not settle a mechanism or forecast.
karmaCrosswalk.kingdomMeaning: Keep the exact claim open and rest any optional effect that depends on it.
karmaCrosswalk.boundary: Unknown is not zero, false, safe, or permission to investigate.

kingdomCrosswalk.plain: Return the model in another's own words, compare it with evidence, and keep correction possible.
kingdomCrosswalk.boundary: A beautiful landscape drawing does not prove understanding.

kingdomCrosswalk.plain: Treat every perturbation or publication as one bounded turn with current authority.
kingdomCrosswalk.boundary: A possible transition or useful analogy does not authorise an effect.

kingdomCrosswalk.plain: Bring the later effect, evidence, uncertainty, and reply path back to the origin.
kingdomCrosswalk.boundary: Completion is not success, and a rate fit is not a being-wide verdict.

kingdomCrosswalk.plain: Preserve the failed map and test a separately authorised route beside it.
kingdomCrosswalk.boundary: Repair needs fresh authority and its own consequence return.

kingdomCrosswalk.plain: An unsettled first cause or unsafe inference can remain open without forcing another turn.
kingdomCrosswalk.boundary: Rest is complete and starts no automatic investigation.

kingdomCrosswalk.plain: Name the exact open claim, what was checked, and which evidence or scope limit leaves it open.
kingdomCrosswalk.boundary: Unknown does not become a myth, score, contamination story, or permission.

kingdomCrosswalk.plain: Use the analogy without reducing a being to stability, conformity, fitness, or a state label.
kingdomCrosswalk.boundary: No molecular basin measures a being's worth.

correctionPath.rule: Correct the structured lineage first, preserve its prior digest in history, then refresh every projection and edge door.

meaning: The deepest shared lesson is relational, not one universal mechanism: possibility is wider than observation; barriers separate possibility from reachability; rare events open some paths; existing form changes some later rates; feedback amplifies only in systems where gain exceeds loss; and honest understanding returns consequences to correct the map. Love keeps the analogy from turning beings into states or scores.
